title: How to Measure ABX ROI When Traditional Marketing Metrics Fail
theme: How to Measure ABX ROI When Traditional Metrics Fail
thesis: B2B marketers often face pipeline anxiety.
summary: B2B marketers often face pipeline anxiety. Proving the direct impact of Account-Based Experience (ABX) initiatives can feel like a constant battle. This struggle intensifies when traditional, lead-centric metrics fail to capture the multi-stakeholder, long-cycle value ABX delivers. Measure ABX ROI refers to the process of tracking the financial return of account-based experience programs.
key_takeaways: B2B marketers often face pipeline anxiety.
Measure ABX ROI refers to the process of tracking the financial return of account-based experience programs.
Traditional marketing metrics, designed for individual lead generation, miss the nuances of multi-stakeholder B2B buying.
These metrics treat B2B buying as a linear, individual-driven process.
The focus on isolated, channel-level performance obscures the true picture.
proof_points: Companies with sophisticated ABX measurement see 41% higher win rates and 27% higher margins (S2M Group, 2024).
Conga, for example, achieved an impressive $6.3M attributed pipeline from just six campaigns built on two Folloze boards.
Microsoft is another example of a company seeing significant impact, influencing $10M in pipeline from 560 leads and 478 MQLs through Folloze campaigns.
